precedence: Part XLV and Appendices BO–BW supersede conflicting earlier boundary/category/axis/coordinate/limit/quality/proof/example/compiler statements; Part XLIV and XLIII retain their stated narrower authorities. Conflicts are flagged, not silently harmonized.

parts.title: Part XXII — Anti-collapse rules
parts.explanation: A concentrated error-prevention layer.
parts.caution: The numbered list crosses a page boundary; use heading boundaries rather than page-only slicing when auditing individual rules.

parts.title: Part XXIII — Glossary
parts.explanation: Defines the working vocabulary needed to keep category, cause, provenance, phenotype and temporal development separate.
parts.caution: Glossary hierarchy/boundary wording must be read under later-authority precedence if Part XLV or Appendices BO–BW conflict with it.

parts.title: Part XXIV — Remaining open questions after the IH revision
parts.explanation: Separates unresolved variables from already-closed defects.
parts.caution: Open questions are not permission to fill gaps by intuition; absent transition or phenotype laws remain explicitly unspecified.

parts.title: Part XXV — Inference matrix for common statements
parts.explanation: A compact claim-status matrix labeling common formulas as core distinctions, axioms, deductions, theorems, rejections or causal inferences.
parts.caution: The matrix states status under the then-current formal core; later-authoritative revisions control if boundary/hyperordinal rules conflict.

parts.title: Part XXVI — Compact canonical formal specification
parts.explanation: Implementation-facing snapshot of the PH-enhanced core.
parts.caution: Use this as a compact local core, not automatically as final authority on later-revised boundary, limit, coordinate or compiler mechanics.

parts.title: Part XXVII — Temporal and developmental logic of Archfemales and Archmales
parts.explanation: A major temporal-developmental formalization.
parts.caution: Do not infer a frozen body from constant Archstage, or Archstage advancement from puberty alone.

parts.title: Part XXVIII — The IH Inheritance Foundation: PA irreducibility, stage recursion, and the transition to explicit phenotype logic
parts.explanation: This transitional foundation consolidates the five-layer ontology: classical inner conditions; irreducible PA developmental modes; composite HGL states; source-sensitive IH inheritance states; and PH whole-profile possession states.
parts.caution: Treat this as the IH/PA foundation for the later PH revision, not as the final phenotype-complete specification where Part XXIX differs.

parts.title: Part XXIX — The PH Phenotype-Possession Revision: authoritative integration
parts.explanation: This is the authoritative PH phenotype-possession integration for the local architecture.
parts.caution: Do not read PH(S) as the complete body state across every ordinary developmental context; it is the source’s HGL phenotype-profile.

parts.title: Part XXX — Biological Metaexpression and the Modal Extension of Hypergendered Logic
parts.explanation: This part makes Biological Metaexpressability explicit by adding the global stage meta-phenotype Γ and stage-relative modal space.
parts.caution: Meta-phenotype is a rule-function over phenotype expression, not merely another ordinary trait.

parts.title: Part XXXI — Final synthesis: the integrated PA–IH–PH–Γ modal architecture
parts.explanation: This synthesis combines PA causal-scope preservation, IH source/provenance preservation, PH whole-profile preservation, Γ global stage metaexpression and stage-relative □/◇ modality into one typed architecture.
parts.caution: This part has a local wording tension around the first Supra stages: the prose mentions inherited/profile structure while the displayed canonical SF1/SM1 formulas remain PA-only; the conflict is preserved rather than silently harmonized.

parts.title: Part XXXII — Macroscopic Anatomical and Outward Phenotypic Expression: authoritative modal correction
parts.explanation: This is an explicit authoritative correction to the modal/metaexpression account: valid Archwomanhood/Archmanhood stages cannot be global only in a microscopic, latent or purely counterfactual sense.
parts.caution: Some stage-governed macroscopic/outward expression does not entail a specific breast, genital, facial, skeletal, body-size or other morphology without a mapping law.

parts.title: Appendix A — Model-theoretic semantics for PA, IH, and PH
parts.explanation: Appendix A supplies a model-theoretic semantics separating causal identity, inheritance/provenance identity and phenotype-profile identity.
parts.caution: Boolean projection can saturate while the full HGL state remains distinct because source/provenance structure is not represented in that projection.

parts.title: Appendix B — De Morgan and scope drills under PA, IH, and PH
parts.explanation: Appendix B is a scope-training suite for De Morgan and operator nesting.
parts.caution: A.8–A.10 appear immediately before the Appendix B heading on the same source pages; preserve that heading-boundary context when citing individual drills.

parts.title: Appendix C — Forty common invalid derivations and why they fail
parts.explanation: Appendix C turns the anti-collapse laws into a catalogue of invalid derivations.
parts.caution: The appendix is pedagogical error analysis: each rejected move is rejected for a specific type/scope/provenance reason, not merely because it is noncanonical.

parts.title: Appendix D — Detailed higher-stage construction: Stages 3 through 10
parts.explanation: Appendix D works the local successor architecture concretely through Stages 3–10 and then shows how to represent much higher finite stages symbolically instead of textually exploding nested structure.
parts.caution: The worked finite stages are examples of the then-current local successor sector; later-authoritative limit/category boundary mechanics remain separately governed.

parts.title: Appendix E — Thirty causal thought experiments
parts.explanation: Appendix E supplies fictional causal thought experiments, explicitly labeled illustrations rather than canon assertions.
parts.caution: The scenarios are examples of possible models, not statements that those tissues, proteins or traits canonically exist.

parts.title: Appendix F — Teaching sequence for lay readers, logicians, scientists, and AI
parts.explanation: Appendix F completes the thought-experiment sequence and reorganizes HGL as a teaching pathway for lay readers, logicians, scientists and AI systems.
parts.caution: The opening E.22–E.30 items continue Appendix E before the formal Appendix F teaching material begins; heading boundaries matter more than page boundaries.

parts.title: Appendix G — Short-form canonical reference sheet
parts.explanation: Appendix G is a one-page canonical reference sheet for the then-current local core: symbols, primitive PA modes, SF1/SM1, the eight-conjunct SF2/SM2 bases, Stage-3+ successor recursion, PA/IH anti-collapse laws, type rules, finite inheritance depth and developmental separation.
parts.caution: Use the reference sheet as a compact snapshot, not as authority over later Part XLV / Appendix BO–BW revisions where they conflict.

parts.title: Appendix H — Proofs and countermodels for stage stagnation
parts.explanation: Appendix H gives direct models and countermodels proving that Archstage and ordinary development are nonidentical variables.
parts.caution: A stage determines a unique phenotype only if a deterministic stage-only phenotype law is additionally supplied; current HGL does not assume such a law.

parts.title: Appendix I — Extended causal deduction and inference catalogue
parts.explanation: Appendix I distinguishes causal deduction from strong but non-theorem causal inference.
parts.caution: Do not convert the appendix’s plausible mechanisms into stage-guaranteed anatomy/physiology unless the source explicitly supplies the needed law.

parts.title: Appendix J — One hundred mini-scenarios for human and AI training
parts.explanation: Appendix J is a large human/AI training set that tests classification of statements about PA, IH, PH, stage, phenotype, inference status, regression/skipping and higher-order structure.
parts.caution: Training-item answers describe the edition’s state at this point; later explicit authority governs any boundary/category/limit statement that was subsequently revised.

parts.title: Appendix K — AI parsing, storage, and theorem-proving rules
parts.explanation: Appendix K translates the formal architecture into machine-readable parsing and theorem-proving rules.
parts.caution: Compiler/parser rules here are an implementation snapshot and are explicitly within the class of statements that later Part XLV / BO–BW may supersede if conflicting.

parts.title: Appendix L — Expanded glossary
parts.explanation: Appendix L expands the glossary around the mature PA–IH–PH/provenance architecture.
parts.caution: Hierarchy/boundary terminology should be crosschecked against later-authoritative category maps if a later appendix explicitly revises the glossary’s wording.

parts.title: Appendix M — Formal resolution of the four major defects identified during review
parts.explanation: Appendix M records formal repairs to four major defects so future revisions do not reintroduce them: Stage-1 category membership is handled by FemaleType/MaleType rather than deriving primitive standalone PA routes; SF2/SM2 are fixed as special eight-term bases; the provisional antithesis bridge is removed in favor of explicit inherited non-opposite states.
parts.caution: Treat the appendix as a defect-history and repair record.
